text:
maria: Quick design review — prototyping a 'stream overlay' that pins a tiny token meter just left of the outgoing chat bubble. stop/regenerate becomes an icon-only pill to save vertical space. landing thoughts?

kevin: left placement seems unobtrusive, but screen-reader and focus order worries. if we hide the textual count visually, how will keyboard users discover it? :thinking_face:

alina: can we try two variants in the prototype: 1) token meter inside the bubble header, 2) token meter pinned outside (like you said). compare visibility + hit target for stop/regenerate.

maria: +1 on A/B. also thinking about the streaming estimate vs final token count — we should show an approximate streaming value (e.g. "~123") and flip to exact when generation ends. prevents users mistaking the stream estimate for a guarantee.

design-bot: uploaded: https://redwood.design/proto/stream-overlay/v2 (proto links only). screenshot shows icon-only stop + tiny counter.

sam: small nit: current keyboard mapping uses Esc to stop + regenerate. that conflicts with browser/back and some editor flows. propose separate bindings: Esc = cancel stream (stop only), Shift+Enter = regenerate. also expose a single keystroke to stop-only — maybe Ctrl+. ?

kevin: accessibility nit — stop button needs an aria-label that reads "Stop generation (S)" and be reachable via tab. If icon-only, ensure visible focus ring and a screen-reader-only text node. Also aria-live region for streaming token updates so AT users get counts without needing to tab repeatedly.

maria: agree. for the aria-live region we should update at a coarse cadence (every 500ms) to avoid overwhelming AT. Also include a short phrase when stream finishes: "Generation complete — final token count: 134".

alina: UX note on the prompt library: current floating drawer overlaps the token meter in small widths. maybe move prompt library toggle into composer rail (left of input) on narrow screens. collapsible.

sam: performance point — the token estimator is slightly laggy when we throttle streaming frames. we can debounce estimator updates separately from UI stream frames to keep token counter responsive. pseudo: ```js
// debounce token updates to 300ms
let last = 0;
function maybeUpdate(n) {
  if (Date.now() - last > 300) { updateCounter(n); last = Date.now(); }
}
```

kevin: copy tweak for the stop/regenerate tooltip: instead of "Stop / Regenerate" use "Stop generation" on hover and reveal a secondary "Regenerate" action in the overflow menu to reduce accidental taps.

design-bot: accessibility checklist added to the prototype doc: focus order, aria-labels, live region cadence, contrast ratios for small numeric badging (. WCAG requires 3:1 for UI components under 18pt).

maria: decision items for next sprint: run small A/B with token meter inside vs pinned; implement aria-live with 500ms throttle; make stop icon have screen-reader text + visible focus; move prompt library toggle to composer rail on narrow widths; change default keyboard mapping (Esc = stop-only, Shift+Enter = regen). I'll file final tickets after this thread. :thumbsup:

kevin: looks good. can we also add a microcopy line under the counter for ambiguous cases: "approximate while streaming"? short, muted.

alina: +1. that clarifies expectation.

sam: will update the keyboard spec and drop a short test plan for SRE to monitor any regressions in streaming latency.

maria: thanks team — I'll toss the prototypes into the design review board and tag you for follow-up. :eyes:
